comparison: Perfect agreement on structural characterization claims (C4, C17-C21). Both evaluations find the size-exclusion chromatography, negative-stain EM, and 3D reconstruction data convincing. Peer reviewers explicitly praise the work as 'very high quality' with 'sound and convincing' conclusions about complex shape and subunit locations.

Strong agreement on localization strategy claims (C37-C50). Both evaluations support the systematic use of tagged constructs for subunit positioning. OpenEval emphasizes stoichiometry evidence from single tag densities (C49), while peer reviewers focus on the effectiveness of multiple tagged constructs for positioning atomic structures.

Strong agreement on cross-linking data (C23-C36). Both evaluations find the cross-linking experiments rigorous and confirmatory. OpenEval highlights validation against crystal structures and appropriate linker distances, while peer reviewers note the cross-linking 'confirms the structural conclusions' with 'redundant and accurate information.'

Disagreement on stoichiometry claims (C49-C50). OpenEval finds single tag densities per construct support stoichiometry claims. Peer reviewers express uncertainty, noting 'little information is given regarding the stoichiometry' and observing heterogeneous particle populations suggesting possible dissociation.

Agreement on uncertainty of functional/mechanistic claims (C61, C63-C64, C66-C67). Both evaluations recognize these as speculative proposals. OpenEval notes they are 'explicitly speculative' requiring experimental validation. Peer reviewers state twice that 'inferences about biochemical function are speculative given the resolution of the structure' at 21 Å.

Disagreement on nucleosome interaction claims (C69-C71). OpenEval finds the ~100 Å distance measurement and histone H3 tail length comparison reasonable structural interpretations. Peer reviewers consider these 'highly speculative,' noting histone tail flexibility means 'one cannot conclude at this stage that PRC2 will bind between two adjacent nucleosomes.'

Partial overlap on structural integration claims (C57-C58). OpenEval supports the rigid-body docking of crystallographic data with EM structure. Peer reviewers group these with functional interpretations they consider speculative, though their primary concern appears focused on mechanistic rather than structural integration claims.

Minimal overlap on AEBP2 coordinating role (C6). OpenEval finds this a reasonable inference from structural and cross-linking data. Peer reviewers include C6 in their group of speculative functional inferences, though their detailed critique focuses more on other mechanistic claims.

OpenEval evaluated background/established knowledge claims (C1-C3, C8-C16, C59, C65, C68) as well-supported by prior literature. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background claims, as peer reviewers focused on novel findings rather than literature citations.

OpenEval evaluated summary/conclusion claims (C7, C72-C74) as proportionate to evidence presented. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addressing these summary statements, though peer reviewers' overall assessment of work quality aligns with supporting the contribution claims.

Minimal overlap on C36 (AEBP2 coordinating role from cross-linking). OpenEval groups this with well-supported cross-linking data. Peer reviewers include it among speculative functional inferences, suggesting different interpretation of whether cross-linking data alone supports functional coordination claims.
